knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Board type changes how a sander removes material, the sequence used and the dust produced, so it is identified before any machine is used.
An unexplained patch next to a possibly painted skirting is a stop point for the pre-start assessment. A solvent test in a closed room and an exploratory sanding are both wrong.
An unidentified species is recorded as unidentified. It is not guessed to fit a limit.
Drilling or cutting can release dust and disturb hazardous material. The warranty distractor is not a stated reason in the lesson.
A product name the client gives is client-reported information and must not be recorded as a confirmed fact.

practicalCriteria: Candidate classifies at least three board samples by edge profile, end grain and width, and records each as identified.
Candidate records the existing finish using visual checks only, with no solvent test in an enclosed space.
Candidate identifies a patch of suspected paint or adhesive on a sample area and stops the simulated job for assessment.
Candidate records the client's product information as client-reported, with the source noted.
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is separate. A knowledge pass does not establish practical competence, and the practical criteria must be observed and recorded by an assessor.
evidenceRequired: Floor identification record with photos of board edges and finish
Client-information record with source and status marked
Assessor observation record of the simulated stop
stopWorkCriteria: Species stated as confirmed without a reliable source
Solvent test carried out in an enclosed room
Sanding started over an unexplained paint or adhesive mark
